t.1.111.1: Even there, abiding in the most excellent austerity, that mighty one became pleasing to behold for the hosts of Siddhas and Cāraṇas.
t.1.111.3: To some he became a brother, to some a friend; and other seers protected him as though he were their son.
t.1.111.2: Eager to serve, free of self-conceit, self-restrained and with his senses conquered, he strove to reach heaven by his own strength, O Bhārata.
t.1.111.4: But Pāṇḍu, having attained after a long time an asceticism free of stain, became like a brahmarṣi, O bull of the Bharatas.
t.1.111.6: We have seen many impassable regions of this mountain, which are the pleasure-grounds of the gods, and likewise of the Gandharvas and Apsarases.
t.1.111.5: Wishing to cross over to the far shore of heaven, he set out from Śataśṛṅga facing north, together with his two wives. There the ascetics, who were themselves going higher and higher up the king of mountains with their faces turned north, spoke to him.
t.1.111.7: the pleasure gardens of Kubera, both level and rugged ground, the banks of great rivers, and the impassable mountain caverns.
t.1.111.8: There are regions of perpetual snow, without trees, beasts or birds; there are some with heavy rains, and some that are impassable and hard to approach.
t.1.111.10: How could these two princesses, who do not deserve hardship, not sink down in exhaustion while journeying upon this king of mountains? Do not go, bull of the Bharatas!
t.1.111.9: Those regions a bird could not cross, how much less other creatures, where the wind alone passed beyond, and the Siddhas and the supreme seers.
t.1.111.11: O blessed ones, they declare that for the childless man there is no door to heaven. Being childless, I am therefore tormented, and that is why I speak to you.
t.1.111.12: Men are born on earth by the hundreds and thousands bound with four debts, those owed to the ancestors, the gods, the seers and men.
t.1.111.13: But the man who does not recognize these at their proper time, for him there are no worlds; this has been established by those who know dharma.
t.1.111.14: With sacrifices one gratifies the gods, with Vedic recitation and austerity the sages, with sons and śrāddha offerings the ancestors, and with kindness one's fellow men.
t.1.111.16: When the body perishes, the destruction of the ancestors is certain; this is the settled conclusion. Therefore the best of men are born here for the sake of offspring.
t.1.111.15: From my debts to the seers, the gods and men I have been released in accordance with dharma, but from the debt to the ancestors I am not released, and for that reason I am tormented, O you whose wealth is austerity.
t.1.111.17: Just as I was begotten in my father's field by that great-souled one, in just that way, how might offspring be born in this field of mine?
t.1.111.18: O righteous one, there is indeed offspring for you, O king; we know it with our divine eye: auspicious, sinless, and like unto the gods.
t.1.111.21: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Having heard those words of the ascetics, Pāṇḍu became absorbed in anxious thought, knowing that his own power to beget offspring had been destroyed by the curse of the deer.
t.1.111.19: O tiger among men, bring about here through your own action what has been ordained by fate; the wise man who remains unperturbed obtains a fruit free from affliction.
t.1.111.20: Since that outcome has been foreseen, dear son, you should make the effort; once you have obtained offspring endowed with virtues, you will find joy.
t.1.111.22: In a secluded place he spoke to Kuntī, his glorious lawful wife, urging upon her the expedient of having offspring begotten in a time of distress.
t.1.111.23: Offspring, indeed, is the foundation in the worlds, joined with dharma: thus, O Kuntī, the wise have known the eternal dharma from the very beginning.
t.1.111.24: Sacrifices offered, gifts given, austerities practised, and vows well observed: all of this, for one who has no offspring, is said here to be not purifying.
t.1.111.25: Having thus understood this, O bright-smiling one, I see clearly, reflecting, "Being childless, I shall not attain the auspicious worlds."
t.1.111.27: These six sons, in the view of dharma, are kinsmen and heirs; and there are six sons who are neither kinsmen nor heirs. Hear of them from me, Pṛthā.
t.1.111.26: Through the curse of the deer my power of begetting has been lost, O timid one, for I was of undisciplined soul and a doer of cruel deeds; it is struck down just as surely as the curse decreed.
t.1.111.28: The son begotten by oneself, the son begotten on one's wife by another, and the son who is bought; the son of a remarried woman, the son born of an unmarried maiden, and the one who is born of a wanton woman.
t.1.111.29: The son who is given, the son who is bought, the son who is adopted, and he who comes of his own accord; the son received along with the bride, the one begotten of seed, and he who is borne in a womb of lower birth.
t.1.111.30: In the absence of each earlier kind, one should, after due reflection, seek to obtain a son of the next. In times of distress, lesser men desire a son from a superior man.
t.1.111.31: The virtuous obtain offspring that yields the fruit of dharma and is superior even to offspring born of one's own seed, O Pṛthā; so said Manu Svāyambhuva.
t.1.111.33: And hear, Kuntī, this story concerning Śāradaṇḍāyanī, the wife of a hero, who was appointed by her elders to bring forth offspring.
t.1.111.32: Therefore today I shall send you forth, since I myself am deprived of the power to beget. Obtain offspring, O glorious lady, from a man who is my equal or my superior.
t.1.111.35: When that rite was completed, she dwelt with that very man, and there she bore three great chariot-warriors, Durjaya and the others.
t.1.111.34: O Kuntī, purified after her monthly course and having bathed, at night at a crossroads, she chose an accomplished twice-born and offered oblations into the fire in the puṃsavana rite for the birth of a son.
t.1.111.36: So you too, O fair lady, at my bidding, quickly make the effort to bring forth offspring by a brāhmaṇa who excels in austerity.
